module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 401

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/401](https://www.erdosproblems.com/401)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos401

/--
Is there some function $f(r)$ such that $f(r)\to \infty$ as $r\to\infty$, such that, for
infinitely many $n$, there exist $a_1,a_2$ with
$$a_1+a_2> n+f(r)\log n$$
such that $a_1!a_2! \mid n!2^n3^n\cdots p_r^n$?

It is ambiguous in [ErGr80] what the intended quantifiers are on the variables (they write 'is
it true that we can find $a_1+a_2>n+f(r)\log n$...'). Comparing to previous problems such as
[728] and [729] it seems most likely that they intended to ask the formulation in the problem
statement.

The answer is yes: Barreto and Leeham have used ChatGPT to provide a proof of the stated problem
(in fact essentially the same construction as their solution to [729]).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos401.lean"]
theorem erdos_401 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r),
        {n : ℕ | ∃ a₁ a₂ : ℕ, 0 < a₁ ∧ 0 < a₂ ∧
          (a₁ : ℝ) + a₂ > n + f r * Real.log n ∧
          a₁.factorial * a₂.factorial ∣
            n.factorial * (∏ i ∈ Finset.range r, Nat.nth Nat.Prime i) ^ n}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos401

sources_consulted: Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), pp. 77–78; https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf

Factorial divisibility with bounded primes beyond the logarithmic barrier: an infinitely-many n result of Erdős type, especially the Problem, Theorem 1, Remark 1, and §7.4; https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1SY_LjPToevYaFl5eNl-rUxJrjrP5u4RC

Pinned local Mathlib sources: Data/Nat/Nth.lean, Data/Nat/Prime/Nth.lean, NumberTheory/PrimeCounting.lean, Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean, Data/Finite/Defs.lean, and the relevant filter definitions.
review.notes: The sole declaration, Erdos401.erdos_401, matches the linked solution paper's explicit quantifiers, strict inequality, positive factorial arguments, and divisibility condition. The original book leaves the n-quantifier implicit, as the docstring acknowledges. Checked that Nat.nth enumerates primes starting at 2, and that the product-power expression equals the product of the first r prime powers. Scratch Lean proofs show that restricting the infinite set to n ≥ 2 is equivalent, so Real.log 0 introduces no defect. Also proved that the linked proof's explicit coefficient tends to +∞, confirming that its conclusion implies the repository statement. The linked proof contains no sorry or custom axioms, but was not rebuilt in its original toolchain. The affirmative solved/Lean status agrees with the linked solution and the independent database. Access limitation: erdosproblems.com/401 and its forum returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers; their current wording and remarks could not be read directly. All experiments were confined to /workspace/review, and the reviewed file's hash still matches the specified commit.
